title: JSON going out and coming back

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. run.js starts the cupboard server, runs your functions against it and prints every request and answer.

tasks.title: Read one show from JSON
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/json.js`, make `showLine(text)` take the JSON text of one show, an object with `name`, `day`, `time` and `presenter` (and sometimes more), and give back one line about it: the name, a comma and a space, the day, ` at `, the time, `, with ` and the presenter, like `'Brass on Sunday, sunday at 11:00, with Gethin'`.

Check calls `showLine` with JSON texts of its own: names with commas and quotes in them, names in another order, and JSON written over several lines.
nextSteps: Print `text` and `typeof text` to see that it is one piece of text.
Turn the text into an object with the method the lesson shows.
Build the line from the object's properties.
Run `node run.js`: the show's name has two commas in it.
hints: Text has no `name` property, so reading `text.name` gives `undefined`. The values are in there, but they have to be read out first.
`JSON.parse(text)` gives back the object the text describes, commas, quotes and all. Read `name`, `day`, `time` and `presenter` from that.
`const show = JSON.parse(text)`, then return `` `${show.name}, ${show.day} at ${show.time}, with ${show.presenter}` ``.

tasks.title: Read every show from the server
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `showNames(base)` ask the server at `base` for the page `/api/shows`, whose body is a JSON list of shows, and give back a list of the names of those shows, in the order the server sent them. When the list is empty, it gives back an empty list.

Check starts a server of its own that answers with shows of its own, and looks at the request its server received and at the list `showNames` gave back.
nextSteps: Send the request and wait for the answer.
Read the body as JSON, not as text, and wait for that too.
Make a new list with the name of each show.
Run `node run.js` and compare the names with the body printed above them.
hints: The body is JSON, so reading it as text gives one long piece of text, not a list of shows.
`response.json()` reads the body and parses it in one go, and needs `await` like `text()`. A list's `map` makes a new list with one value for each item.
`const shows = await response.json()`, then `return shows.map((show) => show.name)`.

tasks.title: Read JSON only when the answer says it is JSON
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `readJson(address)` ask for the page at `address` and look at the type in the answer's `content-type`, the part before any `;`:

- when the type is `application/json`, in small or capital letters, give back the value read from the body
- for any other type, or no content-type at all, give back `null` without reading the body as JSON
- when the answer says it is JSON but its body is not, do not catch the error: the error from reading it comes out of `readJson`

Check starts a server of its own that answers with JSON, with plain text that looks like JSON, with a web page, with a type that only starts like JSON's, with no content-type, and with a body that says JSON and is not.
nextSteps: Send the request and read the `content-type` of the answer.
Take the type out of it: the part before the semicolon, trimmed, in small letters. Remember an answer with no content-type.
Read the body as JSON only when it is, and give back `null` otherwise.
Run `node run.js`: one answer is JSON, one is plain text, and `/api/now` says JSON and is not.
hints: `response.json()` never looks at the content-type. Whether to call it is your decision, made from the header.

`headers.get('content-type')` gives `null` when there is no such header, and the value may have `; charset=utf-8` after the type. `split(';')[0]` keeps the part before the semicolon, and `trim()` and `toLowerCase()` tidy it.
`const type = (response.headers.get('content-type') ?? '').split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()`, then `if (type !== 'application/json') return null`, and otherwise `return await response.json()`.
